ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a substituted transition-state structure, containing two R groups; at the upper right there is an aldehyde fragment, showing a C=O double bond and bearing an explicit H; OH is connected to the middle carbon, several explicit H are also marked in the figure, and there are curved arrows. According to the problem statement, ignore all arrows. Reasoning: Count only bonds for which neither endpoint is hydrogen. The countable bonds are: upper R–C, 1; C–C from that upper carbon to the central carbon, 1; C–C from the upper carbon to the aldehyde carbon, 1; aldehyde C=O, 1; lower R–C, 1; C–C from the lower carbon to the central carbon, 1; C–O from the central carbon to O, 1. Exclude all C–H and O–H bonds. Therefore, the total is 7.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a substituted transition-state structure with two R groups, an aldehyde C=O at the upper right, an OH attached to the central carbon, explicit H labels, and curved arrows. Disregard the arrows as instructed. Then enumerate only bonds whose two endpoints are not hydrogen: upper R–C, C–C down to the central carbon, C–C to the aldehyde carbon, C=O, lower R–C, lower C–central C, and central C–O. Exclude C–H and O–H bonds. The resulting count is 7.
